composition_parti.rule: Composition is picturesque-asymmetrical: openings follow the plan behind them, apparent rhythm is coincidental, and it is usually broken by the garage bay at one end and the entry mass at the other.
composition_parti.note: Fixes a cascade bug: the resolved kit previously inherited 'strict-bilateral-odd-bay' (eclectic-revivals + colonial-revival, via the family splice), which directly contradicts this node's own stated symmetry attribute.

variants.note: The two-storey multi-gabled mass is the style's default skeleton (massing_affinities, cross-gable-victorian, common), arrived at by additive plan growth rather than picturesque intent.
The 1965-1980 neo-mansard subtype, a device for concealing a second storey or apartment bulk (lineage: references second-empire, weight 0.3).
Overrides the cascade's inherited value (shingle-style, via colonial-revival's family). No member text or exemplar names a gambrel roof.

roof_form.rule: Multiple gables of near-equal width and identical pitch, with no dominant roof form -- 'the eye cannot find a primary roof and the building has no top' (long description, 'gable proliferation'). Maximum three gables per principal elevation; the dominant gable must exceed the next largest by not less than 25 percent in width (hard constraint c04).
roof_form.note: Direct quote of defining_characteristics item 4 and constraint c04. Fixes a cascade bug: the previously-resolved gambrel roof is Shingle Style's own device, unrelated to this node.

roof_pitch.rule: Four to seven gables per principal elevation, pitches identical at 8:12 or 10:12.
roof_pitch.note: Direct quote of typical_ratios. Fixes a cascade bug: the previously-resolved 'pitch_min=9:12, pitch_typical_range=[9,14]' is queen-anne-american's own steep-Victorian figure (via the family splice), overshooting this node's own documented pitch band at the top end and misstating it as a minimum rather than the flat, uniform figure the style actually uses.

eave_condition.rule: Shallow eave and rake overhang, typically 6 to 12 in -- 'overhangs of six to twelve inches, leaving no shadow line, which forces every applied detail to grow in size and colour contrast to remain visible' (long description, eave collapse).
eave_condition.note: Direct quote of defining_characteristics item 8. Fixes a cascade bug: the previously-resolved shingle-style eave rule (via the family splice) happens to share a similar ceiling but is sourced from an unrelated style and omits this node's own causal point about why the ornament reads loud.

variants.note: Applied to the street elevation and required to return not less than 24 in onto the side before terminating (hard constraint c01) -- the return-failure is the node's single most named diagnostic.
The three non-street elevations, per defining_characteristics item 3.

Overrides the cascade's inherited value (shingle-style, via colonial-revival's family). Shingle Style's whole discipline is a continuous shingle field wrapping every elevation and corner without exception; neo-eclectic's defining move is the opposite -- masonry on the front only, cladding change at the corner -- and is a large part of why the two nodes are structurally opposed.

primary_cladding.rule: Masonry or stone applied to the street elevation only, with vinyl or panel siding on the remaining three. A masonry veneer must be applied to all elevations of the mass it clads, or terminate at an inside corner or a change of plane of not less than 24 in; a return of less than 24 in onto a side elevation is forbidden (hard constraint c01).
primary_cladding.note: Direct quote of defining_characteristics item 3, diagnostic_tells item 1 ('Brick front with a 6-to-12-inch return onto the side elevation, then vinyl'), and constraint c01. Fixes a cascade bug: shingle-style's continuous-field rule (inherited via the family splice) is the structural opposite of what this node actually does and what it is diagnosed by.

material_change_rule.rule: A masonry veneer must be applied to all elevations of the mass it clads, or terminate at an inside corner or a change of plane of not less than 24 in. A return of less than 24 in is forbidden and is the style's single most-named failure: 'brick or stone covers the front elevation and turns the corner by six to twelve inches before giving way to vinyl, which announces that the masonry is a face rather than a wall.'
material_change_rule.note: Direct quote of constraint c01 and the long description's own naming of 'material return failure' as the first of its seven named failure modes.

color_strategy.rule: Ornament, being applied in shallow extruded polymer, vinyl, or aluminum with no shadow depth, relies on size and colour contrast rather than profile to remain legible -- the mechanism the node's own text gives for why the ornament 'looks loud.'
color_strategy.note: Direct paraphrase of the long description's 'eave collapse' paragraph. Marked judgment because the node does not state a literal colour-strategy rule; this restates its own causal argument about contrast substituting for shadow, one register up from where it is stated (trim, not body colour).

window_type.rule_append: No more than two distinct window shapes on one principal elevation; three or more -- rectangular, arched, half-round, octagonal, on a single wall -- is this style's own named diagnostic overreach, not a canonical target (diagnostic_tells item 4).
window_type.note: Adds a clause the inherited double-hung-sash binding (british-picturesque, via the family splice) does not carry. Marked judgment: the node's own text names the three-or-more-shapes condition as a failure to diagnose, not as an explicit numeric ceiling, so the two-shape cap is an inference from that diagnostic rather than a directly stated rule.

variants.note: 'A half-round or "Palladian" window filling a gable, unrelated in width to anything below it' -- present and characteristic, but named as a diagnostic tell of scale failure, not a canonical target to reproduce uncritically.

special_window.rule: Where a special window occurs it is a half-round or Palladian assembly filling a gable, frequently at 1.5 to 2 times the scale the wall beneath it can actually carry.
special_window.note: Direct quote of diagnostic_tells item 3 and typical_ratios ('Entry element 1.5 to 2 times the height of the adjacent wall opening').

as_built_door_width_pct_diagnostic.note: 'Garage doors 32 to 48 ft of a 50 to 60 ft frontage -- 55 to 80 percent, against the 33 percent that a coherent frontage tolerates.' Recorded as the style's own documented as-built violation, not a target.

garage_strategy.rule_append: Three-car garages must be split or turned (c05) -- this node's own sharper form of the family's shared 33-percent-width ceiling.
garage_strategy.note: Extends the family's already-correct attached-set-back-or-side-loaded binding with this node's own additional c05 clause and its own diagnostic as-built figures, which the family kit (necessarily blending all three members) does not carry at this precision.

variants.note: 'Motifs are quoted -- pediment, keystone, fanlight, dentil, shutter, Palladian window -- with no transmission of the proportional system that generated them' (lineage note against colonial-revival).
The defining absence. distinguished_from[colonial-revival]: 'Neo-eclectic quotes the same motifs without the system.'

order.rule: Where classical order-derived elements appear they are selected from a printed elevation menu and applied to a plan generated independently of them, never derived from a declared module or column diameter.
order.note: Fixes a conceptual cascade bug, not just a numeric one: the resolved kit inherits colonial-revival's genuine, module-derived order (ionic-scamozzi) as though this node runs the same system. That contradicts the node's own defining argument -- procedural decoupling of elevation from plan -- which is the entire reason this node exists as distinct from colonial-revival. Direct quote of the lineage entry against colonial-revival and the long description's opening paragraph.

ornament_vocabulary.rule: Two or more unrelated historical grammars quoted on a single building, or one grammar quoted at incorrect scale: Colonial, French Country, Craftsman, and neo-Mediterranean packages selected from a printed menu labelled A through F, not generated from any one coherent proportional system.
ornament_vocabulary.note: Direct quote of defining_characteristics item 2 and the long description's founding definition of the node.

entry_element_height_ratio.note: The style's own documented as-built condition -- an oversized two-storey foyer volume -- not a target to reproduce.

entry_sequence.rule: A two-storey entry element with a half-round or Palladian assembly, opening into a twenty-foot volume in a plan twelve to fourteen feet wide: entry inflation is the fifth of the node's own seven named failure modes and is recorded here diagnostically, not prescriptively.
entry_sequence.note: Direct quote of typical_ratios and the long description's 'entry inflation' paragraph. Marked judgment/diagnostic because this parameter documents an observed excess, not a design target -- see the schema's own `diagnostic` field, used here as intended.

variants.note: Overrides the cascade's inherited value (english-georgian, via colonial-revival's family). Real classical-depth trim is precisely the thing this node's own text names as what neo-eclectic quotes and fails to deliver.

trim_family.rule: Trim of minimal profile depth in extruded polymer, vinyl, or aluminum, compensating with size and colour contrast for the absence of shadow -- against 'three to six inches in the sources quoted.'
trim_family.note: Direct quote of defining_characteristics item 6 and typical_ratios.
